title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 20 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and adversaries: china, russia, iran.

stories.h: Estonian drone company targeted in sabotage attempt as part of ‘Russia’s hybrid war against Europe’: Prime Minister Michal
stories.what: Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said in a statement on X that the attack was “GRU-ordered,” an abbreviation for the Russian military intelligence agency.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: Chinese anti-tank missile spotted in Morocco
stories.what: Officer cadets at Morocco’s Royal Military Academy fired a Chinese HJ-9A anti-tank missile from an American-made Humvee during a graduation shooting exercise this month, according to images shared by Chinese military commentator Dianbo.
stories.you: Ground robots are moving from demos to real orders, starting with logistics and dangerous jobs.

stories.h: ‘Davidson Window’ Admiral Hopes He Was Wrong On China’s Ability To Take Taiwan By 2027
stories.what: The time frame Adm. Philip Davidson famously declared China could be ready to invade Taiwan is about to arrive.
stories.you: Allies' wars and budgets are the testing ground and a big second market for new defense tech.

stories.h: Navy eyes ‘operational employment’ of key UUV programs, admiral says
stories.what: The Navy is expected to receive its third Orca prototype vessel “soon,” according to a service official.
stories.you: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

stories.h: 10,000 Swiss sniper rounds smuggled into Russia
stories.what: At least 110,000 rounds of Swiss sniper ammunition reached Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, smuggled through Slovenia and Kyrgyzstan despite a Swiss export ban, the Swiss newspaper NZZ am Sonntag reported.
stories.you: What China, Russia and Iran field sets the requirements the Pentagon buys against.

watch.h: Stopgap funding expires: FY27 appropriations or another CR
watch.why: December 11. Decides whether DAWG's $54.6B and Golden Dome's growth become real money.

idea.h: Contract intelligence and capture agent for small vendors
idea.why: An LLM agent that watches SAM.gov, DIU, OTA consortia, budget documents and portfolio acquisition executives, matches openings to a product, and drafts responses. Thousands of new vendors are navigating DAWG and the new acquisition rules; turning valuations into orders is the stated test.
